entries.name: Courtside Deck
entries.concept: An evidence-first review deck with simultaneous decisions. A cool frame holds a white decision sheet beneath the match. Browsing places the source map to the left of a compact rally list.
interactions: Keep/remove and serve remain visible together; bounds and Next are separate lower actions.
Editor / Rallies pill switches experience with a visible return path.
Play / pause advances a local simulated source clock.
Keep / remove and near / far decisions remain selected through navigation.
Next review visits the remaining flag-derived queue, then shows completion.
Browse exposes every fixture rally as a start-frame card; selecting one seeks immediately.
Source-proportional vertical rail collapses and restores; clicking a gap enters the mock full Editor.
Bounds supports start/end steppers in 0.1 s increments and continuous range dragging.
Find missed rally enters the full Editor in a gap; add creates a local rally and Return to Rallies keeps it.
Outside-phone Review / Browse / Bounds controls and matching screen query parameters preview states; Reset restores the fixture.

direction.question: Should this rally be kept, and which court side serves?
direction.face: A low-chroma cool frame takes its temperature from the court illustration; the volleyball mark identifies the product.
direction.signatureElement: The two unresolved review flags become two explicit decision rows, beside a computed queue-progress strip.

acceptedWarnings: Lint numbering is zero-padding for timestamps only.
Inspector hero-void at 1440px is the deliberate surrounding space around the brief-required max-width 430px app canvas.

appScreenCritique: The court leads the reading order; the white lower sheet makes the review choices and next action easy to locate.
Review rows, bounds and next action share sheet edges. Browse rail plus list closes the full width with no orphan column.
Teal is confined to the source/time data and progress, with monochrome decision controls.
The selected score, card score, duration and source position are rendered from the same rally object; totals come from flags and rows.
The initial 0/4 progress is empty, with four pending items; missing serving side says unconfirmed.
Rail segments use start and duration divided by full source duration. Gaps remain source time and can open the Editor.
All requested states fit at 360 and 390 pixels; the canvas centers at 430 pixels on wider pages.

direction.question: What decision does this rally still need?
direction.face: An ink-only score and an open worksheet establish the face; blue appears only on time/source data.
direction.signatureElement: Clip and Serve tabs encode the two independent review flags, and the next unresolved question opens after a clip choice.

acceptedWarnings: Lint numbering is zero-padding for timestamps only.
Inspector hero-void at 1440px is the deliberate surrounding space around the brief-required max-width 430px app canvas.

appScreenCritique: The image carries the evidence, while one large question at the bottom limits competing decisions.
The two decision targets and two footer actions use paired equal widths, and browse rows align their scores on a common right edge.
The chrome stays achromatic; blue marks source and trim data, and the primary action stays near-black.
Scores, review flags and times use the shared fixture. A completed decision does not silently resolve the other flag.
Unchecked decision circles and unconfirmed labels distinguish missing judgments from an explicit Keep.
The right source rail retains proportional durations and a single current-position mark; the score is outside the film for legibility.
Both questions, the browse list, bounds and Editor fit the three requested widths with touch targets at least 44 pixels tall.

entries.concept: A larger true-black film surface leads into a compact bottom dock. Serving side and bounds sit above the keep/remove/advance row; larger thumbnail rows and a right source map serve browsing.

direction.question: Can this point be checked while keeping the match in view?
direction.face: True black carries the media, a drawn volleyball mark names the product, and sport lime marks source/time data.
direction.signatureElement: The film-first surface and compact decision dock organize the review around the selected point, while lightness alone separates the lower work sheet.

acceptedWarnings: Lint numbering is zero-padding for timestamps only.
Inspector hero-void at 1440px is the deliberate surrounding space around the brief-required max-width 430px app canvas.

appScreenCritique: The film has the greatest emphasis and the lower dock keeps the next action within the same thumb area.
Rounded lower surfaces group decisions without shadows or borders; thumbnail rows share one media slot and one score edge.
Black, #111 and #2a2a2a provide depth; lime appears on source/time data while selected decisions invert to white.
All counts and scores come from the fixture or current local state; selection changes the film clock and active card together.
Initial progress has no stub at zero; pending side choices stay unselected and become explicit white selections.
The vertical rail uses the same time scale and marks as the other alternatives; full-source gaps remain navigable.
The bounds spacing was tightened after screenshot review to keep 44 pixel slider targets and all actions visible at 360 pixels.

dataInventory: VolleySplice is a portrait volleyball highlight editor.
Practice match is the shared synthetic project scope.
Cedar and Harbor are the two shared team names.
The source lasts 1,560,000 ms, shown as 26:00.
The initial position is 770,400 ms within rally 18.
Rally 18 starts at 766,200 ms and ends at 782,800 ms.
The selected score is Cedar 9 : 8 Harbor.
The 36 rallies retain their fixture numbers, bounds and scores.
Rallies 18, 19, 23 and 27 need clip and/or serving-side review.
The main job is resolving those independent flags, then navigating and correcting the full source.

validationSummary.screenshotsInspected: Review, Browse, Bounds and Editor contact sheets at 360, 390 and 768 pixels, plus Taste inspector renders.
validationSummary.t3Screenshots: Unavailable after two attempts; T3 navigation and evaluate-based interaction checks succeeded.
validationSummary.screenshotFallback: Assigned Taste skill local headless Chrome CDP inspector and explicit viewport captures.

limitations: Synthetic local prototypes; no video decoding, analysis, audio, export, upload, message or backend action.
The provided court illustration is intentionally repeated for every start-frame preview; simulated time changes a clock rather than the illustration.
Choices and added rallies persist within a page session and reset on reload or the outside Reset button.
A rally added in a gap uses the preceding rally score and serving side as sample values; no actual score or serve inference is performed.
T3 raw screenshot limitation, repeated twice: Preview snapshot failed: Preview automation snapshot timed out after 15000ms.
The mock full Editor supports source scrubbing and local rally addition only; it is not the production Editor.
Native Android builds and real-media usability were not tested because application source was outside this experiment scope.
